source.title: Fine-grained Optimization of Deep Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including supplemental material, is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports image-classification error results for a training and weight-renormalization method, comparing them with baseline training; this bears on V4's optimizer/generalization comparison but does not directly compare adaptive optimizers with SGD.
record.gate_note: Reported benchmark errors for FG-SGD and baseline Euclidean training are included. Other manifold variants and architecture results are also reported, but are not rows because the claim versions do not directly test their named comparisons. Theoretical generalization bounds and cited prior-work results are not empirical rows.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates constrained weight manifolds and FG-SGD, but none of its comparisons measures a claim version. Its adaptive step size does not constitute a comparison of Adam-like adaptive optimizers against SGD under V4. Weight-norm bounds and manifold curvature do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness or its correlation with generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that FG-SGD with collections of constrained weight manifolds can improve CNN convergence properties and benchmark classification performance. Their convergence guarantees depend on stated assumptions; global convergence applies to particular network classes.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes FG-SGD with weight renormalization and manifold constraints; it does not use the original interventions in the listed claim versions. It compares its method with Euclidean baseline training.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported performance differs by dataset, architecture, manifold collection, data augmentation, and weight-grouping scheme.

fits_no_version.finding: Table III reports ImageNet classification error of 24.73 ± 0.32% for Euclidean ResNet-50 training and 22.89 ± 0.08% for PIO with sphere, oblique, Stiefel and Euclidean weight spaces.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training CNNs with FG-SGD on collections of constrained weight manifolds can lower held-out classification error relative to Euclidean baseline training.

record.problems: The main reported evidence is classification error, not training-test generalization gaps. No random-label capacity check is reported. For several tables, the relationship between slash-separated values and individual configurations depends on table headings; no such values are used here.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained: although the paper reports numerical classification errors comparing FG-SGD variants with Euclidean baselines, none measures a behavior named by the claim versions. In particular, the optimizer comparison does not test adaptive optimizers against SGD under V4's stated tuning conditions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and training recipe.
Test error across widths beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, including weight-decay and optimizer-switching interventions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and interventions that recover large-batch performance.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its relationship to training-test gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T2 classification and V4 tested_not_extracted status. Keeping the rows empty is appropriate, and rows_left_out already declares the omitted method-performance comparisons.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out natural-label generalization.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test-error behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local-connectivity controls.

The paper compares FG-SGD to baseline Euclidean training and reports test errors, but it does not compare adaptive optimizers such as Adam with SGD or momentum SGD, so these results do not measure V4's stated behavior.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout interventions and their effect on test error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to training-test gaps.
Removing influential memorized examples and retraining.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
